Hi Laura,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

- What we heard: two primary use cases (support triage + automated knowledge base summarization) and target latency/cost constraints for pilot.
- Proposal: 4-week pilot (10k monthly queries), Redwood-hosted instance using a curated open model + prefix caching to stay within latency SLOs.
- Success criteria: avg latency < 600ms for 95th pct, relevant-accuracy on your eval set > 85%, and a plan to productionize if metrics look good.

Next steps from our side:
1) I'll share a short SOW + standard service agreement for legal to review.
2) Marissa will coordinate pricing and spot any contract items you may want flagged.
3) If helpful, we can run a 30-minute session with your procurement/legal to walk through the commercial terms and security controls.

If you can share the procurement contact or the right person on legal, we'll route the docs there. Otherwise I'll send the SOW and our standard SA to the group.

Attaching: Redwood_Service_Agreement_v1.pdf (standard SA).

Best,

Hi Laura — bumping this thread to check whether Kate/procurement had a chance to review the redlines. Wanted to offer a couple things that often help move these along:

- We can schedule a quick 20-30m call with our contracts and engineering to walk through any technical/operational asks (common sticking points are data retention and audit log access).
- If timing is the blocker, we're usually able to accept a short-term pilot addendum (30 days) to unblock procurement while counsel finishes final language.

Jonas (cc'ed) is our legal lead and can join the call if that helps.

Can you share an expected timeline or a good time for a short sync this week? Happy to coordinate with Kate and procurement.

Thanks —
Ben

Thanks for the bump, Ben — looping in the thread to nudge procurement and counsel.

Laura/Kate/procurement — quick note from our side on two pragmatic paths to keep the pilot on track:

1) Full redline review: We can schedule 30 minutes with Jonas (contracts) + our security lead to walk through the specific redline items. We find that talking through data classification, retention windows, and breach notification timelines reduces back-and-forth.
2) Pilot addendum option: If procurement needs to start the pilot sooner, we're happy to put a 30-day pilot addendum in place under our standard SA terms (no production SLAs) while counsel finalizes the full SA. This is commonly accepted by enterprise customers to hit business timelines.

If you prefer, Jonas can draft suggested language for the items Kate flagged and we'll send a tracked version back to you by EOD tomorrow. Otherwise, share a couple of available times for a short sync and we'll coordinate.
